models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Benign and very light - Portorosa to Lipari tomorrow is a 22 nm motor-sail, best off the dock at 06:00.
briefing.synopsis: The payload shows no organised pressure feature over the islands: winds everywhere are under about 5 kt with land-breeze style direction swings, backing and veering between SE overnight and N/NE by midday (ECMWF IFS 0.25°, 03 Oct 00Z, and ICON-2i, 03 Oct 00Z). Portorosa consensus for tonight and tomorrow runs 3-5 kt with interval-maximum gusts to 9-14 kt, and seas stay at 0.1 ft on both MFWAM and ECMWF WAM (both 03 Oct 00Z). Through 05 Oct the pattern slowly establishes a light NW-N flow across the island group, still only 4-6 kt. I do not have a synoptic chart or pressure values in the payload - this is read off the wind and wave fields only.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: Tonight is Portorosa Marina, which scores as fully sheltered - enclosed basin, all-round protection - with 4.2 kt SE, gusts 8.6 kt and 0.1 ft swell from the NNW (ECMWF IFS, 03 Oct 00Z). There is no realistic trigger to move the fleet; nothing in the payload approaches a threshold. Normal dock lines and fenders, and expect the breeze to drift round to the SE/S through the small hours.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Recommended departure is 06:00 with roughly 4.7 kt SSE, gusts to 10.9 kt and 0.1 ft seas - a dead run on the 342°T track, so plan on motoring or motor-sailing (ECMWF IFS, 03 Oct 00Z; ICON-2i, 03 Oct 00Z). The window is effectively open all day: every two-hourly slot from 06:00 to 14:00 computes 'go' at 2-5 kt, with the breeze going light ENE around midday (2.1 kt) before filling NNE at 4-5 kt in the afternoon. Nothing deteriorates later in the day, so 06:00 is about arrival timing and berth availability at Lipari rather than weather.

passage_notes.note: 4-5 kt SSE at 06:00 easing to 2 kt ENE midday, then NNE 4-5 kt; seas 0.1 ft throughout. IFS gusts of 11-13 kt against a 3-5 kt mean are interval maxima in light air, not squalls. Motoring passage - budget fuel and time, roughly 3 h in the published windows.
NW 4-5 kt, gusts under 12 kt, 0.1 ft seas; close to beam reach all day. Any window 06:00-14:00 works; 12:00-14:00 has the most breeze at 5.0-5.4 kt.
NW 4.6-6.3 kt, gusts to 13.6 kt, seas 0.2-0.3 ft. Best sailing angle on the 12:00 window (6.3 kt NNW, close reach), but a 06:00-08:00 start keeps the arrival early.

passage_notes.leg: Stromboli → Panarea, optional return (06 Oct, 11 nm, 219°T)
passage_notes.note: Very light, 3 kt all day with gusts under 6 kt and 0.5 ft seas. Motoring leg whichever window you take.
S/SE 4-7 kt, seas 0.5-0.7 ft. The 14:00 slot is the windiest at 6.9 kt ESE on a broad reach, but a 28 nm leg argues for the 06:00 start.
S 4-7 kt, seas 0.7-0.8 ft, beam to close reach. Easiest leg of the week in these numbers.
The one leg with real breeze: 10-13 kt SSW-S, gusts 14-20 kt, seas 0.9-1.2 ft, mostly close hauled. Still computes 'go', but it is five days out and worth re-briefing.

cautions: Portorosa on arrival 09 Oct shows 15.4 kt SW gusting 20.4 kt (ECMWF IFS, 03 Oct 00Z) - the marina is enclosed, but plan the berthing approach for breeze. Long lead time, treat as a trend only.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli (05 Oct) rates only 'workable': it is open from every direction and flagged no-anchoring, so shelter there depends entirely on conditions staying calm - 3.8 kt NNW and 0.5 ft swell in the current run.
Gust figures from ECMWF IFS are interval maxima, not instantaneous, so the large gust-to-mean ratios in light air (e.g. 13 kt against 4 kt tomorrow midday) read worse than they will feel.
briefing.confidence_note: No leg or berth in the payload carries a models_range_kt flag, meaning IFS, AIFS and ICON-2i agree within 6 kt everywhere, and forecast stability at 0-24 h lead shows mean wind shifts of only 0.3-0.4 kt between runs - though direction in such light air still wanders 18-23° run to run.
